items.stem: A contractor discovers a ground condition it believes entitles it to more time and money, but the contract requires written notice within 14 days of becoming aware. It serves notice after 30 days. What is the typical consequence?

options.text: The entitlement may be lost or reduced because a condition precedent notice was missed
options.rationale: Correct: where notice is a condition precedent, late service can bar the claim.
Many standard forms make timely notice a condition of recovery.

options.text: The contractor is automatically entitled to double the claim
options.rationale: Late notice does not increase entitlement; it risks losing it.

options.text: The employer must serve the notice instead
options.rationale: The burden to serve the entitlement notice is on the contractor.

items.explanation: Correct: where notice is a condition precedent, late service can bar the claim.

items.stem: Which TWO are typically true of a design-and-build procurement route? (Select TWO.)

options.text: Design responsibility is transferred to the contractor
options.rationale: Correct: the contractor takes responsibility for completing and often developing the design.

options.text: The employer usually has a single point of responsibility
options.rationale: Correct: a single contractor is responsible for both design and construction.

options.text: The employer retains full control over detailed design throughout
options.rationale: That is more typical of a traditional route, not design-and-build.

options.text: There is never any employer's requirements document
options.rationale: Employer's requirements are central to defining the brief under design-and-build.

items.explanation: Correct: the contractor takes responsibility for completing and often developing the design.

items.stem: A site engineer verbally tells a trade to add two extra doors. No written instruction follows. Under a standard form, what is the safest commercial position before proceeding?

options.text: Obtain a compliant written variation instruction before carrying out the work
options.rationale: Correct: a compliant instruction protects valuation and payment entitlement.

options.text: Proceed immediately; verbal instructions are always binding
options.rationale: Verbal instructions often need written confirmation to be valued as variations.

options.text: Treat it as defect correction at no cost
options.rationale: Added scope is a variation, not correction of defective work.

options.text: Ignore it because extra doors cannot be a variation
options.rationale: Added scope can be a variation; the issue is securing the instruction.

items.explanation: Correct: a compliant instruction protects valuation and payment entitlement.
